subject: science
passage: The okapi—a shy, forest-dwelling mammal of central Africa whose striped back legs make it look a little like a ______ is actually the closest living relative of the giraffe. Like a giraffe, it has a long, dark tongue that it uses to strip leaves from branches. European scientists did not formally describe the species until 1901. Because it lives deep in dense rainforest, the okapi is still rarely seen in the wild.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The subject "The okapi" goes with the verb "is." Everything from "a shy, forest-dwelling mammal" to "zebra" is extra information, and it opens with a dash. It must close with a matching dash, even though the comma in "shy, forest-dwelling" may make a comma look tempting.
explanation.A: Incorrect. A semicolon would cut the subject "The okapi" off from its verb "is," and neither side would be a complete sentence.
explanation.B: Correct. The second dash closes the pair around the extra information, so "The okapi" connects to "is."
explanation.C: Incorrect. Without a closing dash, the extra information is never set off, and "a zebra is" wrongly seems to be the subject and verb.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Extra information that opens with a dash can't close with a comma; the two marks must match.
